topics.title: AI didn't shrink the job market — it rerouted it into concrete and copper
topics.why: The Economist's ~1M AI-driven jobs figure is mostly electricians, HVAC, and data-center construction crews, not tech roles — a sharper story than the usual 'AI creates jobs' headline.

topics.title: The layoff blame game: AI-cited cuts are up 199% this month, but most were coming anyway
topics.why: Researchers are now openly calling out companies using AI as convenient cover for layoffs they'd have made regardless — worth teaching readers how to read a layoff headline.

topics.title: Half of enterprises now call their AI rollout a disappointment
topics.why: New survey data: 48% call gen-AI adoption a letdown (up from 34%), with only 29% seeing real ROI — a look at where that gap sends budgets, and jobs, next.

topics.title: AI-skills jobs are growing 8x faster than the market — here's exactly which skills
topics.why: 69% growth vs 9% overall isn't one skill, it's a specific cluster — a practical breakdown for a knowledge worker deciding what to learn next.

topics.title: The C-suite's new two-tier company: 92% grooming an 'AI elite' while 60% plan to cut everyone else
topics.why: A stark internal bifurcation story — what it actually looks like to be on either side of that split inside a company right now.
